chunks: From him, from Musa ibn Ja'far ibn Wahb, from Dawud ibn Mahziyar, from 'Ali ibn Isma'il, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I said to Abu Ja'far عليه السلام: A man saw something in his sleep and experienced pleasure and desire, then he rose and did not see anything on his garment. He said: Then he said, If he is ill, then ghusl (ritual bath) is obligatory upon him; and if he is healthy, then there is nothing upon him.

key_terms.اللَّذَّةَ: sensory pleasure experienced in the dream
key_terms.الْغُسْلُ: the ritual bath required for major ritual impurity
key_terms.صَحِيحًا: being healthy and free from illness
key_terms.مَرِيضًا: being ill or in a state of sickness

ai.seo_question: Does a person have to perform ghusl (ritual bath) after a dream if no trace is found?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a person who experiences pleasure and desire in sleep but finds no trace afterward. Imam Abu Ja'far عليه السلام distinguishes between the sick and the healthy person, requiring ghusl (ritual bath) for the former while imposing nothing on the latter.
